items.title: Ask HN: ERP system suggestions
items.snippet: We are looking to transition to a new ERP system. We've been running the same software since the 70's, and it has been highly customized over time. We'd like to invest in a platform that allows us to modify all aspects of the system, while also starting out with a base that doesn't necessitate starting from scratch (i.e. prebuilt accounting, payroll, etc functions). Preferably the system has an open API for extending the system as necessary, and integrating with third party software. Any suggestions? We are in the metal wholesaling business.

items.snippet: We currently use PNC but their online interface is atrocious/broken and we have frequent problems transferring money. Furthermore, our experiences at their local branch have been disappointing. Our needs are basic: - Single checking account with debit card for each co-founder - Send invoices online - Make (sometimes international) payments - Quickbooks integration - Local branch in Denver, CO (not strictly necessary) We're considering Wells Fargo. Does anyone have experience with them? We also use Gusto for payroll but are worried they won't be around in a few years. What has your experience with Intuit been like?

items.title: Ask HN: Building KasirCepat, an offline-first POS for Indonesia
items.snippet: I'm building KasirCepat, a POS application for small shops in Indonesia. Many of these businesses have unreliable internet connections, so I started with a local-first architecture instead of cloud-first. The main goal is to make the daily workflow simple: - selling products, - tracking inventory, - viewing sales history. I'm curious how other developers approach: - data synchronization, - multi-device workflows, - handling conflicts, - designing software for non-technical users. Especially interested in lessons from building local-first/offline-first applications.
